lots.guide_summary: All six surviving close entries are Gowans SOLD hammers for small sterling spoon lots of 20g to 51g, $40 to $110 AUD (about $1.20 to $2.75 per gram). No exact same-item (Dublin fiddle pair) sale and no UNSOLD found. The only ASKING entry (UK dessert spoons, AUD 275 at GBP 1 = AUD 1.8983) is a category guide and sits outside the range.
lots.working: Keep: no exact same item; lowest surviving close SOLD (plain sterling spoons, last 24 months) = $40 (lots 438749 and 371711); 40 / 1.198 = 33.39, round down to $30. Flip: likely resale about $80 hammer (39.2g at about $2 per gram, the middle of the Gowans close SOLD results), less 15% selling fees ($12), no postage if re-offered locally = $68; 68 / 2.396 = 28.38, round down to $25. The weight-matched results ($60 to $110) suggest $30 will probably be outbid; that is the cost of the strict rule. Melt is a floor only and I could not confirm today's silver spot.
lots.confidence_reason: Dublin hallmarks read clearly in the photo and several opened Gowans SOLD results, but none is the same item, the date letter cycle is not confirmed, the maker mark is unread, and the weight is from the title only.
lots.dropped_entries: Silvershop Dublin EUR 90 teaspoon (page returns 404, snippet only, not verified). Nigel Williams Silver GBP 220 set of six (page returns 403, snippet only, kept only as a lead: about AUD 70 per spoon asking). MyFamilySilver relabelled from close to category guide (dessert spoons, not teaspoons). Researcher's 1860s date is not supported: see key_photo_findings.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please confirm the weight of 39.2g, read the maker's mark, and say how bad the dent in the second bowl is. Are the terminals engraved or have initials been removed?
lots.key_photo_findings: Marks on both spoons read: crowned harp, Hibernia, lower case b date letter in a shield, and Queen Victoria's head duty mark, with a worn script maker's mark below. That is Dublin. The duty mark means before 1890, so lower case b points to the late 1840s (about 1847 to 1848) rather than the 1860s, but I have not checked the Dublin letter table. Maker mark too worn to read. Second spoon has a clear dent in the bowl edge. Both bowls and terminals are scratched; the terminal fronts show scratching that may be erased initials.
lots.condition: Worn, scratched, one bowl dented; hallmarks crisp.

lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD (multi-watch lot with a men's Omega, last 24 months) = $185 (lot 406534); 185 / 1.198 = 154.42, round down to $150. Flip: sum-of-parts resale from Gowans SOLD evidence about $300 (square De Ville head $150 to $200, logo-dial Omega $100 to $130 given single-Omega lows of $130, Seiko and the rest $20 to $50), less 15% fees ($45) and about $30 postage for several parcels = $225; 225 / 2.396 = 93.91, round down to $90. Pottle AUD 550 and Danielle Elizabeth AUD 1,000 (snippet only, the-saleroom search page, not item pages; better watches). eBay USD 198 to 475 asking (snippet only, eBay is closed to us). Researcher's USD rate of 1.50 was assumed; Frankfurter gives USD 1 = AUD 1.4331 (13 Oct 2026), though no USD entry survives.
lots.question_for_gowans: Do any of the watches run? Does the square Omega De Ville head have its crown and caseback, and is the movement Omega? What is the logo on the round Omega's dial (presentation watch)? Can you name the makers of the cushion watch and the ladies watches?
lots.key_photo_findings: Square gold-plated OMEGA De Ville Quartz head with date, no strap. Round gold-plated OMEGA quartz date on worn black lizard-grain strap, dial printed with a company or club logo (presentation piece, lowers collector value). Gold-tone Seiko automatic day-date on a two-tone bracelet, dial worn. Vintage rolled-gold cushion watch on an expanding bracelet with a badly crazed dial. Three small ladies watches (one on an expanding strap, one on a frayed blue fabric strap); brands not legible. All dirty, plating wear.
lots.condition: Worn and dirty, working order unknown; dials of the vintage pieces deteriorated.
